title: Mitra, who holds up men and the earth and the sky

words.meaning: of Mitra, the god of alliance and agreement

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «श्रोतुं योग्यं यशो»; Bhāskara: «श्रवः अन्नं यशो वा»

words.gram: adj., acc. sg. (used of the neuter śravaḥ)

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «चित्रं श्रवः कीर्तिर्यस्यासौ चित्रश्रवाः, अतिशयेन तादृशस्»

sandhi.rule: visarga before ś stays (the Taittirīya writes it as a doubled ś); -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o
final m before c becomes the palatal nasal

samasa.vigraha: चित्रं श्रवः यस्य सः चित्रश्रवाः, अतिशयेन चित्रश्रवाः

morphology.note: no verb is stated; Sāyaṇa supplies «अस्ति»: ‘great is the fame of Mitra’.

translation.literal: Of Mitra, supporter of the peoples, of the god, the winnable fame, true, most brilliantly famed.
translation.readable: Great is the glory of Mitra, the god who upholds all peoples: a glory that brings reward, true and most splendid.

words.meaning: sets in order, makes each take up his task

words.context: Bhāskara: «प्रजानन् तत्तदधिकारानुरूपविधानज्ञः», knowing what each is fit for

words.meaning: the peoples, those who till the land

words.context: Bhāskara: «अनिमिषा अनिमिषेणादरेणा»; or ‘the unwinking ones’, the gods

words.meaning: may we offer, let us worship with

sandhi.rule: final n before m is unchanged; -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o
-īḥ before a vowel becomes -īr; ā + a becomes ā
m before gh becomes ṅ; t before v becomes d

morphology.note: the perfect of √धृ with the reduplicating syllable lengthened (दा- for द-), a Vedic form; the perfect here states a lasting fact.
instrumental of the root noun अनिमिष् ‘not-blinking’; Bhāskara also allows it as a plural, ‘the unwinking gods’.

translation.literal: Mitra, knowing, sets people in order; Mitra has held up the earth and the sky; Mitra watches the peoples unblinking; to the true one let us offer an oblation with ghee.
translation.readable: Mitra, who knows, sets each person to his task; Mitra holds up the earth and the heavens; Mitra watches over all peoples without ever closing his eyes. To him, the true, let us offer our oblation rich with ghee.

sandhi_exceptions.note: मर्तः + अस्तु: -aḥ becomes -o and the a of astu is kept (मर्तो अस्तु), a Vedic hiatus inside the pāda (P. 6.1.115 (प्रकृत्याऽन्तःपादमव्यपरे)).
अंहः + अश्नोति: likewise अंहो अश्नोति, with the a kept.

words.role: main verb of the first clause

words.meaning: rich in offerings; endowed with strength
words.role: predicate: ‘let him be rich in offerings’

words.meaning: by (your) ordinance, by keeping the vow

words.role: first predicate of the second line

words.meaning: helped by you, protected by you

sandhi.rule: -e before a vowel becomes -a, leaving a hiatus

morphology.note: the desiderative of √शक् ‘to be able’, used in the Veda for ‘to try to help, to serve’.

translation.literal: Let that mortal stand forth rich in offerings, O Mitra, who strives for you, O Āditya, by your ordinance. He, helped by you, is not slain, not overpowered; distress does not reach him from near or from afar.
translation.readable: Mitra, son of Aditi, let the one who serves you by your law be foremost and rich in offerings. Protected by you he is not slain, not overcome; no trouble reaches him, near or far.

meaning: Three ṛks to Mitra, the god of the morning and of agreements between men. The first praises his glory; the second says what he does — he sets each person to his work, holds up earth and sky, and watches over everyone without blinking; the third promises that the one who serves him by his ordinance is safe from harm near or far. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the first verse is used in making the fire-pan (Sāyaṇa: Mitra is chosen to calm it, «वारुण्युखाऽसीद्धा मैत्रियोपैति शान्त्यै»), and the three together stand among the offering verses of TS 3.4.11; in the Ṛgveda they are 3.59.6, 3.59.1 and 3.59.2. In the morning Sandhyā the worshipper stands before the rising Sun and greets him as Mitra.
in_the_rite: Morning sūryopasthāna: the three ṛks are recited standing, facing the rising Sun, after the Gāyatrī has been given leave. The Mylapore prayoga gives the viniyoga: the All-gods as seers, gāyatrī and triṣṭubh the metres, Mitra the deity, used in the upasthāna of the morning Sandhyā (vin-mitrasya).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the first verse at TS 4.1.6, supplies the verb ‘is’: «मित्रस्य देवस्य श्रवः श्रोतुं योग्यं यशो महदस्तीति शेषः», and explains the choice of Mitra: the blazing fire-pan is fierce, Varuṇa’s, and Mitra’s verse calms it — «अभिद्धा प्रज्वलिता येयमुखा सेयमुग्रत्वाद्वारुणी, तस्या मैत्र्यच शान्तिर्भ-वति».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on TS 3.4.11: Mitra moves people to act knowing what each is fit for — «जनान् सर्वान् यातयति चेष्टयति प्रजानन् तत्तदधिकारानुरूपविधानज्ञः» — and ‘watching’ means helping: «आभिमुख्येन पश्यति उपकरोतीत्यर्थः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The first ṛk is a gāyatrī, the other two triṣṭubhs — hence the viniyoga’s ‘gāyatrī and triṣṭubh’. The Ṛgveda (3.59.6) reads the first verse differently: «मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतो ऽवो देवस्य सानसि द्युम्नं चित्रश्रवस्तमम्» — avaḥ ‘help’ for śravaḥ ‘fame’, and dyumnam ‘splendour’ for satyam. The Taittirīya and the prayogas have श्रवः and सत्यम्.

notes.label: historical
notes.text: Ṛgveda 3.59 is the one hymn of the Ṛgveda addressed to Mitra alone; the Sandhyā recites its sixth, first and second verses in that order.
